topic.subject: social
topic.title: Traders, kings and pilgrims; the Gupta age
topic.scope: Silk Route, trade with Rome, Kushanas, Samudragupta prashasti, Harshavardhana, Fa Xian and Xuan Zang, Pallavas and Chalukyas

concepts.name: The Silk Route and Ancient Trade

misconceptions.statement: The Silk Route was a single paved road made of silk.
misconceptions.why: Students interpret the name literally based on modern road infrastructure.
misconceptions.fix: The Silk Route was a vast network of interconnected land and sea paths used for trading many goods, not just silk.

probe.question: Why was the Silk Route called that if they also traded gold and spices?
probe.wrong_answer: Because the road was made of silk fabric so it would be soft for the horses.

misconceptions.statement: Ancient trade was only between India and Rome.
misconceptions.why: Textbooks often highlight the Roman trade specifically, leading students to ignore other regional partners.
misconceptions.fix: India traded with many regions, including Southeast Asia, China, and the Middle East, not just the Roman Empire.

probe.question: Did Indian traders only sell their goods to people in Rome?
probe.wrong_answer: Yes, because the book says India had a big trade relationship with Rome.

misconceptions.statement: A prashasti is a perfectly factual biography of a king.
misconceptions.why: Students often assume historical documents are as objective as modern news reports.
misconceptions.fix: A prashasti is a poem or inscription written by court poets to praise the king, often exaggerating his achievements.

probe.question: If a prashasti says a king never lost a battle, is it definitely true?
probe.wrong_answer: Yes, because it is an official record written by a poet in the king's court.

misconceptions.statement: All kings in the Gupta age ruled the entire Indian subcontinent.
misconceptions.why: Students struggle with the concept of fragmented power and overlapping regional kingdoms.
misconceptions.fix: The Gupta empire was large, but many other independent kingdoms like the Pallavas and Chalukyas ruled simultaneously in different regions.

probe.question: Who was the ruler of South India during the time of the Gupta empire?
probe.wrong_answer: Samudragupta, because he was the main king of that time.

misconceptions.statement: Pilgrims like Fa Xian and Xuan Zang traveled to India to conquer land.
misconceptions.why: Students conflate all historical travelers with invaders or military figures.
misconceptions.fix: Pilgrims traveled to India specifically to visit holy sites and study Buddhism, not to rule or capture territory.

probe.question: Why did the Chinese pilgrims come to India?
probe.wrong_answer: They came to fight the kings and take over the land.
